Subject: RE: Internal: NovusAI 429 spike — can SRE confirm root cause and mitigation

Hi team — quick technical summary and immediate remediation we applied.

What happened (root cause):
- Yesterday (2027-06-06) during a routine policy rollout we introduced a new burst-window mapping that intended to tighten per-tenant short-window buckets for fairness. Unfortunately the mapping logic had an off-by-one in the aggregation boundary for combined streaming + chat sessions.
- When requests with both streaming frames and a long token history landed, the enforcement path double-counted a small subset of tokens across two overlapping windows. That made the effective token usage appear higher than the configured per-tenant burst allowance and triggered 429 enforcement for about ~3% of requests.
- The miscount only materialised for tenants sending large batches of long-context requests and those using the streaming v2 path — which matches NovusAI’s traffic pattern.

What we did (mitigation):
- 09:50 PT — rolled back the burst-window mapping to previous stable config (rl_config_diff.txt attached).
- 10:07 PT — applied a hotfix to the enforcement code to prevent double-counting on overlapping window boundaries (support_log_snippet.txt attached).
- 10:20 PT — monitoring showed 429s returning to baseline for affected tenants.

Next steps (postmortem items):
- Short-term (by 2027-06-09): add unit tests that simulate streaming+chat overlap and add a monitoring alert for sudden per-tenant enforcement deltas.
- Medium-term (by 2027-07-01): audit burst-window rollout tooling to add a canary filter for high-history sessions.
- We will provide the raw deltas and log snippets for your audit.

We’re classifying this as a config-rollout regression with a code-path edge-case. No customer data was exfiltrated; this is an availability/regulatory incident only.

Attachments: [attachment: rl_config_diff.txt (text)], [attachment: support_log_snippet.txt (text)]

—Soojin

Subject: Post-incident summary & remediation plan — NovusAI 429s (08:25–08:47 PT)

Hi Elena / Tom — thanks again for flagging this. Below is a short post-incident summary and our proposed remediation and customer goodwill offer.

Summary:
- Incident: unexpected 429s from 08:25–08:47 PT on 2027-06-07 caused by a burst-window mapping regression that double-counted tokens for streaming+chat overlap.
- Impact: ~3% of requests for NovusAI (higher in staging), briefly increasing client-side retry rates and causing a small uptick in latency for affected sessions. No failed writes, no data loss, no security events.
- Root cause: rollout of a new burst-window aggregation rule with an off-by-one boundary that double-counted tokens when streaming frames plus long context co-occurred.

What we fixed (timeline):
- 09:50 PT — rolled back the burst-window mapping to known-good config (rollback ID: rb_20270607_01).
- 10:07 PT — deployed an enforcement hotfix to eliminate double-counting edge case.
- 10:20 PT — metrics returned to baseline and we opened a postmortem ticket (SUP-7891).

Customer remediation and offer:
- Operational: we will credit NovusAI for the affected time window equivalent to one week of committed peak capacity (applied to your next invoice).
- Evidence: we will provide the config delta, log excerpts, and a short unit-test artifact demonstrating the regression and fix.
- Follow-up: SRE will share the specific monitoring alert and the timeline for medium-term tooling changes by 2027-06-09.

Action items for Redwood (responsible / due):
- SRE (Soojin) — unit tests and monitoring alert (due 2027-06-09).
- Product (Jasmine) — add canary rollout requirement for burst-window policy (due 2027-07-01).
- Account (Marcus) — confirm credit and deliver postmortem package (due 2027-06-09).

Please let me know if the credit offer works for you and if you need any additional logs or a deeper timeline. We’ll also share the postmortem folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-postmortem-notes

Again, apologies for the disruption — we take availability incidents seriously and will do what’s needed to make this right.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
